description: TourismFireWatch uses NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data to visualize fire activity near selected tourism destinations. We aim to build a map and dashboard supporting environmental awareness and tourism emergency preparedness. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, satellite data, geospatial analysis, AI/ML, data visualization, research, and science communication.
summary:
TourismFireWatch is a satellite-data-driven project designed to connect NASA fire observations with tourism-related geographic awareness. Using active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite products through the Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), the project aims to provide an accessible way to explore fire hotspots, historical activity, and their geographic context around tourism destinations.

The project processes and harmonizes observations from multiple satellite sources while preserving sensor-specific information. Its planned interactive dashboard supports geographic exploration, date-based filtering, regional analysis, and tourism-location context.

By making satellite observations easier to understand, TourismFireWatch aims to support environmental awareness, tourism research, and more informed planning. It is an informational tool, not a wildfire prediction system or an official emergency alert satellite.
details: TourismFireWatch focuses on identifying and visualizing forest fire activity near tourism destinations, initially focusing on Murree, Pakistan. The project uses NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations to explore fire hotspots and their spatial and temporal patterns. The proposed system organizes fire observations into a common format and presents the information through geographical maps, historical patterns, and calendar-based visualizations. Its main benefit is to improve environmental awareness and help tourists, local communities, and emergency responders understand periods and locations of increased fire activity. The project combines NASA Earth observation data with geospatial analysis and data visualization. It aims to connect forest fire monitoring with tourism safety and environmental preparedness. An important limitation is that satellite hotspot detections do not automatically confirm an actual wildfire. Further verification is needed before treating a detection as a confirmed fire.
